241: **Section 2.06 Withholding**
242: 
243: Buyer and the Company shall be entitled to deduct and withhold from any amounts payable pursuant to this Agreement such amounts as Buyer, the Company, or the Escrow Agent may be required to deduct and withhold under the Code, or any applicable provision of state, local, or non-U.S. Tax Law, with respect to the making of any such payment. To the extent that amounts are so withheld and remitted to the applicable Governmental Authority, such withheld amounts shall be treated for all purposes of this Agreement as having been paid to the Person in respect of which such deduction and withholding was made.
244: 
245: **Section 2.07 Closing**
246: 
247: The closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the \"Closing\") shall take place remotely via the electronic exchange of documents and signatures on the date that is three (3) Business Days after the date on which all of the conditions set forth in Article VII have been satisfied or waived (other than those conditions that by their nature are to be satisfied at the Closing, but subject to the satisfaction or waiver of such conditions at the Closing), or at such other time, date, and place as the Parties may mutually agree in writing (the \"Closing Date\"). The Parties anticipate that the Closing will occur in mid-January 2026. The Closing shall be deemed to be effective as of 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on the Closing Date.

The Escrow Fund shall be held, invested, and disbursed by the Escrow Agent in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement. The Escrow Fund shall serve as security for Seller\'s indemnification obligations under Article IX and the post-Closing adjustment obligations under Section 2.04, as and to the extent provided herein and in the Escrow Agreement.

**(d)** *Repayment of Closing Indebtedness.* At or promptly following the Closing, Buyer shall cause the Company to repay, discharge, and satisfy in full all Closing Indebtedness. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Buyer in connection with the repayment of such Closing Indebtedness.
**Section 2.04 Post-Closing NWC Adjustment**

**(a)** *Closing Statement.* Within ninety (90) days following the Closing Date, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the \"Closing Statement\") setting forth Buyer\'s good-faith calculation of the actual (i) Closing NWC, (ii) Closing Indebtedness, and (iii) Transaction Expenses, together with reasonable supporting documentation, schedules, and work papers. The Closing Statement shall be prepared in accordance with the Accounting Principles and in a manner consistent with the preparation of the Estimated Closing Statement. Buyer shall provide Seller and its Representatives with reasonable access, during normal business hours and upon reasonable prior notice, to the books and records of the Company and the work papers used in the preparation of the Closing Statement.

**(b)** *Review and Objection.* Seller shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of the Closing Statement (the \"Review Period\") to review the Closing Statement. During the Review Period, Buyer shall provide Seller and its Representatives with reasonable access to the books and records of the Company, the work papers of the Company\'s accountants, and the personnel of the Company, in each case to the extent reasonably necessary for Seller\'s review of the Closing Statement. If Seller does not deliver a written notice of objection (an \"Objection Notice\") to Buyer within the Review Period, the Closing Statement as delivered by Buyer shall be deemed final and binding on the Parties. If Seller delivers an Objection Notice within the Review Period, such Objection Notice shall specify in reasonable detail each item in dispute (each, a \"Disputed Item\"), the basis for such dispute, and the amount Seller believes to be the correct amount. Any item or amount not specifically identified as a Disputed Item in the Objection Notice shall be deemed accepted by Seller and shall be final and binding on the Parties.

**(c)** *Resolution of Disputes.* If Seller delivers a timely Objection Notice, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith for a period of twenty (20) Business Days following delivery of the Objection Notice (the \"Resolution Period\") to resolve all Disputed Items. If the Parties are unable to resolve all Disputed Items within the Resolution Period, any remaining Disputed Items shall be submitted for final resolution to an independent, nationally recognized accounting firm mutually agreed upon by Buyer and Seller (the \"Independent Accountant\"); *provided* that such firm shall not be Winslow & Tate CPA Group, the auditors of the Company, or any accounting firm that has provided services to Buyer or Seller during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to such engagement. The Independent Accountant shall be engaged to resolve only the remaining Disputed Items and shall determine the correct amount of each such Disputed Item in accordance with the Accounting Principles, and such determination shall be final and binding on the Parties, absent manifest error. The Independent Accountant shall not assign a value to any Disputed Item that is greater than the highest value or less than the lowest value claimed by either Party. The Independent Accountant shall render its written determination within thirty (30) days after such engagement and shall set forth in such determination a reasoned basis for its resolution of each Disputed Item. The fees and expenses of the Independent Accountant shall be allocated between the Parties based on the relative amounts of the aggregate Disputed Items resolved in favor of each Party (as determined by the Independent Accountant), such that the Party whose positions are furthest from the Independent Accountant\'s determinations bears a proportionally greater share of such fees and expenses.
**(d)** *Adjustment Payment.* Within five (5) Business Days after the final determination of the Closing Statement (as determined pursuant to this Section 2.04):

> \(i\) If the Purchase Price as finally determined (using the actual Closing NWC, Closing Indebtedness, and Transaction Expenses as finally determined) exceeds the Purchase Price as calculated using the Estimated Closing Statement, Buyer shall pay such excess amount to Seller by wire transfer of immediately available funds.

> \(ii\) If the Purchase Price as calculated using the Estimated Closing Statement exceeds the Purchase Price as finally determined, Seller shall pay such excess amount to Buyer (first, by instructing the Escrow Agent to release such amount from the Escrow Fund, and, to the extent the Escrow Fund is insufficient, by wire transfer of immediately available funds from Seller directly to Buyer).

All adjustments pursuant to this Section 2.04 shall be made on a dollar-for-dollar basis from the first dollar of any difference, without any collar, threshold, or de minimis amount. Any adjustment amounts payable under this Section 2.04 shall bear interest from the Closing Date through the date of payment at the prime rate as published in *The Wall Street Journal* on the Closing Date (or, if the Closing Date is not a Business Day, on the immediately preceding Business Day), calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed.
**Section 2.05 Earnout**

**(a)** *Maximum Earnout Payment.* If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period (the twelve (12) month period ending December 31, 2026) equals or exceeds Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), Buyer shall pay to Seller an amount equal to Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) (the \"Maximum Earnout Payment\").

**(b)** *Pro-Rata Earnout.* If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period is at least Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000) but less than Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), Buyer shall pay to Seller an amount (the \"Earnout Payment\") equal to: (\$25,000,000 ÷ (\$38,000,000 -- \$32,000,000)) × (Actual Adjusted EBITDA -- \$32,000,000). For the avoidance of doubt, this formula results in a linear interpolation, such that the Earnout Payment increases by approximately Four Million One Hundred Sixty-Six Thousand Six Hundred Sixty-Seven Dollars (\$4,166,667) for each One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) of Adjusted EBITDA in excess of \$32,000,000. If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period is less than \$32,000,000, no Earnout Payment shall be due or payable.

**(c)** *Earnout Calculation and Dispute Resolution.* Within sixty (60) days after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the \"Earnout Statement\") setting forth Buyer\'s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period, together with reasonable supporting documentation. Seller shall have thirty (30) days to review the Earnout Statement and deliver any objections thereto. The dispute resolution procedures set forth in Section 2.04(b) and Section 2.04(c) shall apply *mutatis mutandis* to any dispute with respect to the Earnout Statement.

**(d)** *Operation of the Business During the Earnout Period.* From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. Without limiting the foregoing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action that would reasonably be expected to reduce the Adjusted EBITDA of the Company below the levels that would otherwise have been achieved. In furtherance of the foregoing, during the Earnout Period, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources as in effect immediately prior to the Closing Date and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Buyer acknowledges and agrees that Seller shall have no obligation to contribute resources, personnel, or funds to the Company during the Earnout Period, and the obligations set forth in this Section 2.05(d) are solely obligations of Buyer.

**(e)** *Payment of Earnout.* Any Earnout Payment determined to be payable pursuant to this Section 2.05 shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period (whether by agreement of the Parties, expiration of the review period without objection, or determination of the Independent Accountant), by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller. For U.S. federal income tax purposes, the Parties agree to treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price.
**Section 2.06 Withholding**

Buyer and the Company shall be entitled to deduct and withhold from any amounts payable pursuant to this Agreement such amounts as Buyer, the Company, or the Escrow Agent may be required to deduct and withhold under the Code, or any applicable provision of state, local, or non-U.S. Tax Law, with respect to the making of any such payment. To the extent that amounts are so withheld and remitted to the applicable Governmental Authority, such withheld amounts shall be treated for all purposes of this Agreement as having been paid to the Person in respect of which such deduction and withholding was made.
**Section 2.07 Closing**

The closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the \"Closing\") shall take place remotely via the electronic exchange of documents and signatures on the date that is three (3) Business Days after the date on which all of the conditions set forth in Article VII have been satisfied or waived (other than those conditions that by their nature are to be satisfied at the Closing, but subject to the satisfaction or waiver of such conditions at the Closing), or at such other time, date, and place as the Parties may mutually agree in writing (the \"Closing Date\"). The Parties anticipate that the Closing will occur in mid-January 2026. The Closing shall be deemed to be effective as of 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on the Closing Date.

**[ARTICLE III]{.underline}**
**[REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF SELLER]{.underline}**
Seller represents and warrants to Buyer as follows:
**Section 3.01 Organization and Good Standing**

Seller is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware. Seller has full corporate power and authority to own, lease, and operate its properties and assets and to carry on its business as presently conducted. Seller is duly qualified or licensed to do business and is in good standing in each jurisdiction where the nature of its business or the ownership or leasing of its properties requires such qualification.
**Section 3.02 Authority; Binding Effect**

Seller has full corporate power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under this Agreement and each other Transaction Document to which it is or will be a party, and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby. The execution, delivery, and performance by Seller of this Agreement and each other Transaction Document to which it is or will be a party, and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby, have been duly and validly authorized by all necessary corporate action on the part of Seller, including approval by Seller\'s board of directors. No other corporate proceedings on the part of Seller are necessary to authorize the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement or to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. This Agreement has been, and at the Closing each other Transaction Document to which Seller is or will be a party will be, duly and validly executed and delivered by Seller and, assuming the due authorization, execution, and delivery by the other parties hereto and thereto, constitutes, or upon execution and delivery will constitute, a legal, valid, and binding obligation of Seller, enforceable against Seller in accordance with its terms, subject to (a) applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, fraudulent conveyance, and similar Laws affecting creditors\' rights and remedies generally and (b) general principles of equity (whether applied in a proceeding at law or in equity).
**Section 3.03 Ownership of Shares**

Seller is the record and beneficial owner of 1,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share, of the Company, which constitute all of the issued and outstanding shares of capital stock of the Company, free and clear of all Encumbrances (other than restrictions arising under applicable securities Laws). There are no outstanding options, warrants, convertible securities, rights of first refusal, rights of first offer, preemptive rights, subscription rights, or other rights, agreements, commitments, or arrangements of any kind relating to the Shares or obligating Seller to transfer or dispose of any Shares. Upon delivery of the Shares to Buyer at the Closing in accordance with this Agreement, Buyer will acquire good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of all Encumbrances (other than restrictions arising under applicable securities Laws and Encumbrances created by or through Buyer).
**Section 3.04 No Conflicts; Consents**

The execution, delivery, and performance by Seller of this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents, and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby, do not and will not (a) conflict with or violate the certificate of incorporation or bylaws (or other organizational documents) of Seller, (b) conflict with or violate any Law or order applicable to Seller or by which any property or asset of Seller is bound or affected, (c) result in any breach of or constitute a default (or an event that, with the giving of notice or lapse of time, or both, would become a default) under, give rise to a right of termination, cancellation, modification, or acceleration of any obligation under, or result in the creation of any Encumbrance upon any of the properties or assets of Seller under, any contract, agreement, instrument, Permit, or other arrangement to which Seller is a party or by which Seller or any of its properties or assets is bound or affected, or (d) require any filing with, notification to, consent, approval, authorization, or waiver of, or any order, registration, or declaration from, any Governmental Authority or other Person, except (with respect to clause (d)) (i) filings required under the HSR Act and (ii) as set forth on Schedule 3.04.
**Section 3.05 Litigation**

There are no Actions pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened against Seller that would reasonably be expected to adversely affect or restrict Seller\'s ability to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents or to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby.
**Section 3.06 Brokers**

Neither Seller nor any of its Affiliates has retained or authorized any broker, finder, financial advisor, investment banker, or other intermediary who might be entitled to any fee or commission in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, except as set forth on Schedule 3.06.
**[ARTICLE IV]{.underline}**
**[REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES REGARDING THE COMPANY]{.underline}**

Seller represents and warrants to Buyer that, except as set forth in the Disclosure Schedules delivered by Seller to Buyer concurrently with the execution and delivery of this Agreement (the \"Disclosure Schedules\"), the following representations and warranties are true and correct as of the date hereof:
**Section 4.01 Organization and Qualification**

The Company is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Oregon. The Company has full corporate power and authority to own, lease, and operate its properties and assets and to carry on its business as currently conducted. The Company is duly qualified or licensed to do business and is in good standing in each jurisdiction where the character of its properties owned or leased or the nature of its business makes such qualification or licensing necessary, including the States of Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. Seller has made available to Buyer true, correct, and complete copies of the articles of incorporation and bylaws of the Company, as currently in effect.
**Section 4.02 Authority**

The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by the Company (to the extent it is a party hereto) have been duly and validly authorized by all necessary corporate action on the part of the Company.
**Section 4.03 Capitalization**

The authorized capital stock of the Company consists of 5,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share, of which 1,000,000 shares are issued and outstanding as of the date hereof. All of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of the Company have been duly authorized, are validly issued, fully paid, and nonassessable, and were issued in compliance with all applicable Laws and in accordance with the Company\'s articles of incorporation and bylaws. There are no outstanding options, warrants, convertible or exchangeable securities, subscriptions, rights (including preemptive rights or rights of first refusal), stock appreciation rights, phantom stock, profit participation, calls, commitments, or agreements of any kind relating to the capital stock of the Company, or obligating the Company to issue, deliver, sell, repurchase, or redeem any shares of its capital stock. There are no outstanding or authorized equity-based awards, stock appreciation rights, phantom stock awards, profit interests, or similar rights with respect to the Company. There are no outstanding agreements, contracts, or commitments restricting the transfer of, or requiring the registration for sale of, any shares of the capital stock of the Company. There are no anti-dilution or similar adjustments with respect to any equity securities of the Company.
**Section 4.04 Subsidiaries**

The Company does not own, directly or indirectly, any equity interest, capital stock, membership interest, partnership interest, joint venture interest, or other ownership interest in any other Person. The Company has no subsidiaries.
**Section 4.05 No Conflicts; Consents**

The execution, delivery, and performance by the Company of this Agreement (to the extent it is a party hereto), and the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, do not and will not (a) conflict with or violate the articles of incorporation or bylaws (or other organizational documents) of the Company, (b) conflict with or violate any Law or order applicable to the Company or by which any property or asset of the Company is bound or affected, or (c) result in any breach of or constitute a default (or an event that, with the giving of notice or lapse of time, or both, would become a default) under, give rise to a right of termination, cancellation, modification, or acceleration of, or result in the creation of any Encumbrance upon any of the properties or assets of the Company under, any contract, agreement, instrument, Permit, or other arrangement to which the Company is a party or by which the Company or any of its properties or assets is bound or affected, except, in each case of clauses (b) and (c), where such conflict, violation, breach, or default would not, individually or in the aggregate, be material to the Company. Schedule 4.05 sets forth a true and complete list of all consents, waivers, approvals, authorizations, and notices required to be obtained or made in connection with the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby.
**Section 4.06 Financial Statements**

Seller has delivered to Buyer (a) the audited balance sheets of the Company as of December 31, 2022, December 31, 2023, and December 31, 2024, and the related audited statements of income, stockholders\' equity, and cash flows for each of the fiscal years then ended, together with the reports thereon of Winslow & Tate CPA Group, independent certified public accountants, and (b) the unaudited balance sheet of the Company as of September 30, 2025, and the related unaudited statements of income and cash flows for the nine-month period then ended (the financial statements described in clauses (a) and (b) above, collectively, the \"Financial Statements\"). The Company does not have any liabilities, obligations, or commitments of a type that would be required to be reflected on a balance sheet prepared in accordance with GAAP, except (a) liabilities reflected or reserved against in the Financial Statements, (b) liabilities incurred since September 30, 2025 in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice (none of which results from, arises out of, relates to, or was caused by any breach of contract, breach of warranty, tort, infringement, or violation of Law), (c) liabilities arising under the executory portions of contracts to which the Company is a party (not resulting from any breach or default by the Company), (d) Transaction Expenses, and (e) liabilities set forth on Schedule 4.07.
**Section 4.08 Absence of Changes**

**Section 4.09 Real Property**
**(a)** The Company does not own, and has never owned, any real property.

**(b)** Schedule 4.09 sets forth a true and complete list of all real property leased, subleased, or licensed by the Company (the \"Leased Real Property\"), including the address, landlord, annual rent, lease term, and renewal options with respect to each such lease. The Company has a valid and enforceable leasehold interest in each parcel of Leased Real Property, free and clear of all Encumbrances (other than Permitted Encumbrances). The Company has good and valid title to, or a valid and enforceable leasehold interest in, all tangible personal property and assets used in the conduct of its business as currently conducted, free and clear of all Encumbrances other than Permitted Encumbrances. Such personal property is in good operating condition and repair (subject to normal wear and tear) and is adequate and suitable for the purposes for which it is presently being used. **Section 4.11 Intellectual Property**

**(c)** *Third-Party Licenses.* Schedule 4.11(c) sets forth a true and complete list of all material licenses, sublicenses, and other agreements pursuant to which the Company is authorized to use any intellectual property of a third party (other than commercially available, off-the-shelf software licensed on standard terms with annual license fees of less than \$50,000). **(d)** *No Infringement.* To the Knowledge of the Company, the conduct of the Company\'s business as currently conducted does not infringe upon, misappropriate, or otherwise violate the intellectual property rights of any third party. **(e)** *Sufficiency.* The Company owns or has a valid right to use all intellectual property that is material to the conduct of the Company\'s business as currently conducted.
**Section 4.12 Tax Matters**

**(a)** The Company has timely filed (taking into account any valid extensions of time for filing) all Tax Returns required to be filed by it. All such Tax Returns are true, correct, and complete in all material respects.

**(b)** The Company has timely paid all Taxes required to be paid by it (whether or not reflected on any Tax Return), and has withheld and remitted to the appropriate Governmental Authority all Taxes required to be withheld and remitted by it.

**(c)** There are no Actions pending or threatened in writing against the Company with respect to any Taxes. There are no outstanding written assessments, deficiencies, or proposed adjustments of any Tax with respect to the Company. No audit, examination, or other administrative or judicial proceeding relating to Taxes of the Company is currently in progress or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened.

**(d)** The Company has not waived any statute of limitations in respect of Taxes or agreed to any extension of time with respect to a Tax assessment or deficiency, which waiver or extension remains in effect.
**(e)** There are no Encumbrances for Taxes upon any of the assets of the Company (other than Permitted Encumbrances for Taxes not yet due and payable).

**(f)** The Company is not a party to, bound by, or obligated under any Tax-sharing, Tax-allocation, or Tax-indemnity agreement or arrangement (other than any agreement entered into in the ordinary course of business the primary purpose of which is not the allocation or payment of Taxes, and other than any agreement with Seller as part of Seller\'s affiliated consolidated group for federal income Tax purposes, which agreement shall be terminated on or prior to the Closing Date).

**(g)** The Company has been included in the affiliated consolidated group (within the meaning of Section 1504 of the Code) of which Seller is the common parent for federal income Tax purposes. **(h)** The Company has not been a party to any \"reportable transaction\" within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.6011-4(b).
**Section 4.13 Material Contracts**

> \(ii\) is an employment, consulting, severance, change-of-control, retention, or similar agreement with any employee, officer, director, or independent contractor of the Company with annual compensation in excess of \$150,000;

> \(v\) contains any non-competition, non-solicitation, exclusivity, most-favored-nation, or similar restrictive covenant;
> \(vi\) involves the licensing of intellectual property (other than commercially available, off-the-shelf software);
> \(vii\) is an equipment lease, capital lease, or financing arrangement;
> \(viii\) relates to Indebtedness; or
> \(ix\) is otherwise material to the business, operations, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company.

**(b)** Schedule 4.13 sets forth a true and complete list of all Company Material Contracts, including, without limitation: (i) the government contracts with Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, Washington Department of Ecology, United States Army Corps of Engineers, and Bureau of Land Management; (ii) the employment agreements with Patricia Huang, Brian Kowalski, Sandra Firth, and David Alarcon; (iii) the Affiliate Lease with Parkside Realty Holdings LLC (\$1,600,000 annual rent); (iv) the subordinated seller note payable to Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. (\$4,500,000); (v) the TerraSpatial Inc. GIS mapping software license (\$180,000 per year); (vi) the senior term loan agreement with Cascade Mutual Bank (\$28,000,000); (vii) the equipment financing facility with Pacific Lease Corp. (\$9,800,000); and (viii) the environmental liability insurance policies with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co.

**(c)** Seller has made available to Buyer true, correct, and complete copies of all Company Material Contracts (including all amendments, modifications, supplements, and side letters thereto). Each Company Material Contract is in full force and effect, is a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, of the other parties thereto, and is enforceable in accordance with its terms. Neither the Company nor, to the Knowledge of the Company, any other party thereto, is in material breach or default under any Company Material Contract, and no event has occurred that, with the giving of notice or the lapse of time, or both, would constitute a material breach or default thereunder.
**Section 4.14 Employees and Employee Benefits**

**(a)** *Employees.* As of the date hereof, the Company employs approximately 340 full-time employees and no part-time employees. The Company is not a party to, nor is it bound by, any collective bargaining agreement or other contract or arrangement with any labor union or labor organization. There are no pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened labor disputes, work stoppages, slowdowns, lockouts, picketing, or strikes, and no union organizing campaigns are pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened with respect to the employees of the Company. The Company is and has been in compliance in all material respects with all applicable Laws relating to labor and employment, including Laws relating to wages, hours, overtime, classification of employees and independent contractors, immigration, equal employment opportunity, non-discrimination, sexual harassment, occupational health and safety, workers\' compensation, and the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act (and any comparable state or local Laws).

**(b)** *Employee Benefit Plans.* Schedule 4.14(a) sets forth a true and complete list of all Employee Benefit Plans. The Company does not sponsor, maintain, or contribute to any \"defined benefit plan\" (as defined in Section 3(35) of ERISA) or any \"multiemployer plan\" (as defined in Section 3(37) of ERISA). The Employee Benefit Plans include a 401(k) defined contribution plan with a four percent (4%) employer matching contribution. Each Employee Benefit Plan has been established, maintained, funded, and administered in compliance in all material respects with its terms and with all applicable Laws, including ERISA and the Code.

**(c)** *Professional Licenses.* Schedule 4.14(b) sets forth a true and complete list of the twelve (12) employees of the Company who hold professional engineer (\"PE\") licenses, including the name, license number, and state of licensure of each such employee. To the Knowledge of the Company, all such PE licenses are in good standing and no Action is pending or threatened to revoke, suspend, or limit any such license.

**(d)** *Key Employees.* The key employees of the Company include Patricia Huang (Chief Executive Officer), Brian Kowalski (Vice President, Operations), Sandra Firth (Vice President, Business Development), and David Alarcon (Chief Safety Officer).
**Section 4.15 Environmental Matters**

**(a)** *Compliance.* The Company is, and during the past five (5) years has been, in compliance in all material respects with all Environmental Laws applicable to its business, operations, properties, and assets.

**(b)** *Environmental Permits.* The Company holds all Environmental Permits necessary for the conduct of its business as currently conducted, and all such Environmental Permits are in full force and effect. Schedule 4.15(b) sets forth a true and complete list of all twenty-three (23) active Environmental Permits held by the Company, including a description of each permit, the issuing Governmental Authority, the permit number, and the expiration date. The Company is in compliance in all material respects with the terms and conditions of all Environmental Permits. No Action is pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened to revoke, suspend, cancel, terminate, modify, or not renew any Environmental Permit.

**(c)** *No Releases.* Except as disclosed on Schedule 4.15(c), there has been no Release of any Hazardous Substance at, on, under, or from any property currently or formerly owned, operated, or leased by the Company, or at any location to which the Company has transported, arranged for the transportation of, or arranged for the disposal or treatment of, any Hazardous Substance, in each case that would reasonably be expected to give rise to any material liability of the Company under any Environmental Law.

**(d)** *No Proceedings.* Except as disclosed on Schedule 4.15(d), there are no Actions pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened against the Company under any Environmental Law, including any claims, orders, directives, or notices of potential responsibility relating to any Release or threatened Release of any Hazardous Substance, or any claim for investigation, cleanup, removal, remediation, response, corrective action, natural resource damages, property damage, personal injury, or fines or penalties under any Environmental Law.

**(e)** *Environmental Reports.* Seller has made available to Buyer copies of all material environmental assessments, audits, studies, reports, analyses, and investigations in the Company\'s possession or control relating to (i) the environmental condition of any property currently or formerly owned, operated, or leased by the Company, or (ii) the Company\'s compliance with Environmental Laws.

**(f)** *Insurance.* The Company maintains environmental impairment liability insurance with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co. with an aggregate policy limit of \$15,000,000 and a per-occurrence limit of \$5,000,000. In addition, the Company carries project-specific environmental liability insurance relating to the Hargrove Industrial Site with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co. with a policy limit of \$10,000,000.
**Section 4.16 Government Contracts**

**(a)** The Company is a party to four (4) active government contracts, each of which is listed on Schedule 4.16, with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, the Washington Department of Ecology, the United States Army Corps of Engineers, and the Bureau of Land Management (collectively, the \"Government Contracts\").

**(b)** Each Government Contract is in full force and effect and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, of the applicable Governmental Authority. The Company is not in material breach or default under any Government Contract, and no event has occurred that, with the giving of notice or the lapse of time, or both, would constitute a material breach or default thereunder.

**(c)** Neither the Company nor any of its directors, officers, or employees is subject to debarment, suspension, proposed debarment, or proposed suspension by any Governmental Authority, or is listed on any excluded parties list maintained by any Governmental Authority.

**(d)** The Company has complied in all material respects with all applicable procurement Laws, regulations, and requirements in connection with the Government Contracts, including, where applicable, cost accounting standards, truth-in-negotiation requirements, and applicable small business subcontracting requirements.
**Section 4.17 Insurance**

Schedule 4.17 sets forth a true and complete list of all material insurance policies maintained by or on behalf of the Company, including a description of the type of coverage, the insurance carrier, the policy number, the coverage limits, the annual premium, and the expiration date for each such policy. All such insurance policies are in full force and effect and all premiums due and payable with respect thereto have been paid. No written notice of cancellation, non-renewal, or material premium increase has been received by the Company with respect to any such policy. There are no material claims pending under any insurance policy that have been denied or disputed by the applicable insurer. The Company\'s insurance policies include those described in Section 4.15(f) with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co.
**Section 4.18 Compliance with Laws**

The Company is, and during the past three (3) years has been, in compliance in all material respects with all applicable Laws. The Company has not received any written notice from any Governmental Authority alleging any violation of, or failure to comply with, any applicable Law that has not been resolved. The Company holds all Permits necessary for the lawful conduct of its business as currently conducted, and all such Permits are in full force and effect.

470:

473: **[ARTICLE V]{.underline}**

475: **[REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF BUYER]{.underline}**
476: 
477: Buyer represents and warrants to Seller as follows:
478: 
479: **Section 5.01 Organization and Good Standing**
480: 
481: Buyer is a limited liability company duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware. Buyer has full limited liability company power and authority to own, lease, and operate its properties and assets and to carry on its business as presently conducted.
482: 
483: **Section 5.02 Authority; Binding Effect**
484: 
485: Buyer has full limited liability company power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under this Agreement and each other Transaction Document to which it is or will be a party, and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby. The execution, delivery, and performance by Buyer of this Agreement and each other Transaction Document, and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby, have been duly and validly authorized by all necessary limited liability company action on the part of Buyer. This Agreement has been, and at the Closing each other Transaction Document to which Buyer is or will be a party will be, duly and validly executed and delivered by Buyer and, assuming the due authorization, execution, and delivery by the other parties hereto and thereto, constitutes, or upon execution and delivery will constitute, a legal, valid, and binding obligation of Buyer, enforceable against Buyer in accordance with its terms, subject to (a) applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, fraudulent conveyance, and similar Laws affecting creditors\' rights and remedies generally and (b) general principles of equity.
486: 
487: **Section 5.03 No Conflicts; Consents**
488: 
489: The execution, delivery, and performance by Buyer of this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents, and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby, do not and will not (a) conflict with or violate the certificate of formation, limited liability company agreement, or other organizational documents of Buyer, (b) conflict with or violate any Law or order applicable to Buyer, or (c) require any filing with, notification to, consent, approval, authorization, or waiver of, or any order, registration, or declaration from, any Governmental Authority or other Person, except (with respect to clause (c)) filings required under the HSR Act.
490: 
491: **Section 5.04 Financial Capability**
492: 
493: Buyer has, and at the Closing will have, sufficient cash, available lines of credit, or other sources of immediately available funds to enable it to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including payment of the Purchase Price, the Escrow Amount, and all other amounts required to be paid by Buyer in connection herewith. Buyer has delivered to Seller true, correct, and complete copies of (a) the executed commitment letter, dated as of \[●\], 2025, from Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. pursuant to which Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. has committed to provide a senior secured credit facility in the aggregate principal amount of \$125,000,000 to finance a portion of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the \"Debt Commitment Letter\"), and (b) the executed equity commitment letter from Whitmore Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. pursuant to which Whitmore Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. has committed to fund equity contributions sufficient, together with the proceeds of the Debt Commitment Letter, to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. The commitments set forth in the Debt Commitment Letter and the equity commitment letter are in full force and effect and have not been amended, modified, terminated, or withdrawn. No event has occurred that, with or without notice, lapse of time, or both, would constitute a breach or default on the part of Buyer under the Debt Commitment Letter or the equity commitment letter.
494: 
495: **Section 5.05 Litigation**
496: 
497: There are no Actions pending or, to the Knowledge of Buyer, threatened against Buyer or any of its Affiliates that would, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to prevent, materially delay, or materially impair the ability of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.
498: 
499: **Section 5.06 Solvency**
500: 
501: Immediately after giving effect to the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including the payment of the Purchase Price and any related financing, Buyer and the Company, on a consolidated basis, will be Solvent. For purposes of this Section 5.06, \"Solvent\" means that, as of the applicable date of determination, (a) the fair saleable value of the assets of such Person exceeds the amount that will be required to pay the probable liability on its existing debts and other liabilities (including contingent liabilities) as they become absolute and matured, (b) such Person will not have unreasonably small capital with which to conduct its business, and (c) such Person will be able to pay its debts and other liabilities (including contingent liabilities) as they mature.
502: 
503: **Section 5.07 Brokers**
504: 
505: Buyer has engaged Ridgeline Advisors LLC as its financial advisor in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. Except for the engagement of Ridgeline Advisors LLC, neither Buyer nor any of its Affiliates has retained or authorized any broker, finder, financial advisor, investment banker, or other intermediary who might be entitled to any fee or commission in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.
506: 
507: **Section 5.08 Investment Intent**
508: 
509: Buyer is acquiring the Shares solely for its own account for investment purposes and not with a view toward, or for sale in connection with, any distribution thereof, or with any present intention of distributing or selling the Shares. Buyer acknowledges that the Shares have not been registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or under any state securities Laws. Buyer is an \"accredited investor\" as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended.
510: 
511: **Section 5.09 Independent Investigation**
512: 
513: Buyer has conducted its own independent investigation, review, and analysis of the business, operations, assets, liabilities, results of operations, financial condition, and prospects of the Company, which investigation, review, and analysis was conducted by Buyer together with its Representatives, including its legal, tax, and financial advisors. Buyer acknowledges that it and its Representatives have been provided with access to the books, records, properties, and personnel of the Company for such purpose. In entering into this Agreement, Buyer acknowledges that it is not relying on any representation, warranty, statement, advice, or information provided by Seller or any of its Affiliates or Representatives except for the representations and warranties expressly set forth in Article III and Article IV of this Agreement and the Disclosure Schedules. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Buyer acknowledges that neither Seller nor any of its Affiliates or Representatives makes any representation or warranty with respect to (a) any projections, forecasts, estimates, or budgets delivered to or made available to Buyer or its Representatives, or (b) except as expressly set forth in Article III and Article IV, any information, documents, or materials delivered to or made available to Buyer or its Representatives in any \"data rooms,\" management presentations, due diligence discussions, or in any other form in expectation of, or in connection with, the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

519: **Section 6.01 Conduct of Business Prior to Closing**
520: 
521: **(a)** From the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date (or the earlier termination of this Agreement in accordance with Article VIII), except as (i) required by applicable Law, (ii) set forth on Schedule 6.01, or (iii) consented to in writing by Buyer (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), Seller shall cause the Company to:
522: 
523: > \(i\) conduct its business in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice in all material respects;
524: >
525: > \(ii\) use commercially reasonable efforts to preserve intact its business organization, relationships with customers, suppliers, licensors, licensees, Governmental Authorities, and other Persons with whom the Company has material business relationships, and to retain its current officers, key employees, and other key personnel;
526: >
527: > \(iii\) maintain in full force and effect all insurance policies of the Company or replacement policies with comparable coverage on terms no less favorable in the aggregate; and
528: >
529: > \(iv\) maintain its books and records in accordance with past practice and in compliance with applicable Laws.
530:

557: > \(xiii\) enter into any non-competition, non-solicitation, exclusive dealing, or similar restrictive covenant agreement.
558: 
559: **Section 6.02 Access to Information**
560: 
561: From the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date (or the earlier termination of this Agreement in accordance with Article VIII), Seller shall, and shall cause the Company and its officers, directors, employees, accountants, counsel, and other Representatives to, upon reasonable prior notice, afford Buyer and its Representatives reasonable access during normal business hours to the Company\'s properties, offices, plants, other facilities, books, records, contracts, documents, and personnel, and shall furnish to Buyer and its Representatives such additional financial, operating, and other information regarding the Company as Buyer may reasonably request; *provided* that (a) such access shall not unreasonably interfere with the normal operations of the Company, (b) such access shall be conducted in a manner that preserves the confidentiality of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, (c) Seller shall not be required to grant access to, or furnish, any information the disclosure of which would (i) violate any applicable Law, (ii) jeopardize any attorney-client privilege or other legal privilege, or (iii) contravene any binding obligation of confidentiality, and (d) all information provided pursuant to this Section 6.02 shall be subject to the terms and conditions of the Confidentiality Agreement.
562: 
563: **Section 6.03 Confidentiality**
564: 
565: The Mutual Confidentiality Agreement, dated as of June 20, 2025, between Seller and Buyer (the \"Confidentiality Agreement\") shall continue in full force and effect in accordance with its terms, and the terms of the Confidentiality Agreement are hereby incorporated herein by reference. If this Agreement is terminated prior to the Closing, the Confidentiality Agreement shall survive such termination in accordance with its terms.
566: 
567: **Section 6.04 HSR Act Filings**
568: 
569: **(a)** Each of Buyer and Seller shall, as promptly as practicable (and in no event later than ten (10) Business Days after the date of this Agreement), file or cause to be filed with the United States Federal Trade Commission and the United States Department of Justice all notifications and other documents and information required to be filed under the HSR Act with respect to the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.
570: 
571: **(b)** Buyer and Seller shall each use their reasonable best efforts to (i) obtain early termination of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act, (ii) comply at the earliest practicable date with any request for additional information and documentary material that may be issued under the HSR Act, (iii) cooperate with the other Party in connection with any filing under the HSR Act and in connection with resolving any investigation or other inquiry of any Governmental Authority under the HSR Act, and (iv) take all actions necessary, proper, or advisable to cause the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act as promptly as practicable.
572: 
573: **(c)** Buyer shall pay all filing fees payable under the HSR Act in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.
574: 
575: **(d)** Each Party shall promptly notify the other Party of any substantive communication with, and any inquiry from, any Governmental Authority in connection with the HSR Act filings, and shall provide the other Party with a reasonable opportunity to review and comment on any substantive written communications to any such Governmental Authority prior to submission.
576: 
577: **Section 6.05 Third-Party Consents**
578: 
579: Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, as promptly as practicable following the date of this Agreement, all consents, waivers, approvals, authorizations, and notices required to be obtained or made in connection with the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby, including those set forth on Schedule 4.05. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Seller and the Company in connection with obtaining such consents. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither Seller nor the Company shall be required to pay or commit to pay any amount to (or incur any obligation in favor of) any Person from whom any such consent or waiver may be required (other than filing, application, or similar fees imposed by any Governmental Authority).
580: 
581: **Section 6.06 Public Announcements**
582: 
583: Neither Party shall, and each Party shall cause its respective Affiliates not to, issue any press release or make any public announcement relating to the subject matter of this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed); *provided* that either Party may make any public disclosure that it believes in good faith is required by applicable Law, any listing or trading agreement concerning its publicly traded securities, or any rule or regulation of any securities exchange or self-regulatory organization, in which case the disclosing Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to advise the other Party prior to making the disclosure and to provide the other Party with a reasonable opportunity to review and comment upon such disclosure.
584: 
585: **Section 6.07 Tax Matters**
586: 
587: **(a)** *Pre-Closing Tax Returns.* Seller shall prepare and timely file (or cause to be prepared and timely filed) all Tax Returns of the Company for any Pre-Closing Tax Period that are due (taking into account any valid extensions) after the Closing Date. All such Tax Returns shall be prepared in a manner consistent with past practice (unless otherwise required by applicable Law). Seller shall provide drafts of such Tax Returns to Buyer for its review and comment at least thirty (30) days prior to the due date for filing (or, if such Tax Return is due less than forty-five (45) days after the Closing Date, as soon as reasonably practicable). Seller shall consider in good faith any reasonable comments provided by Buyer. Seller shall timely pay or cause to be paid all Taxes shown as due and payable on such Tax Returns.
588: 
589: **(b)** *Straddle Period Tax Returns.* For any taxable period that includes, but does not end on, the Closing Date (each, a \"Straddle Period\"), the Taxes of the Company attributable to the portion of such Straddle Period ending on and including the Closing Date (the \"Pre-Closing Straddle Amount\") shall be determined using a \"closing-of-the-books\" methodology as of the end of the Closing Date, except that Taxes imposed on a periodic basis (such as real property Taxes) shall be allocated to the Pre-Closing Straddle Amount based on the number of days in the Straddle Period falling on or before the Closing Date relative to the total number of days in such Straddle Period.
590: 
591: **(c)** *Transfer Taxes.* All transfer, documentary, sales, use, stamp, registration, value-added, and other similar Taxes and fees (including any penalties and interest) imposed in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (collectively, \"Transfer Taxes\") shall be borne equally by Buyer and Seller. The Party required by applicable Law to file the Tax Return with respect to any Transfer Tax shall file such Tax Return in a timely manner, and the other Party shall promptly reimburse such filing Party for its allocable share of such Transfer Tax.
592: 
593: **(d)** *Cooperation.* After the Closing, Buyer and Seller shall cooperate fully, as and to the extent reasonably requested by the other Party, in connection with the filing of Tax Returns of the Company and the conduct of any audit, litigation, or other proceeding with respect to Taxes of the Company. Such cooperation shall include the retention and, upon the other Party\'s request, the provision of records and information that are reasonably relevant to any such Tax Return, audit, litigation, or other proceeding, and making employees available on a mutually convenient basis to provide additional information and explanation of any material provided hereunder.
594: 
595: **(e)** *Tax Elections.* Neither Buyer nor the Company shall, without the prior written consent of Seller (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), (i) make or change any Tax election with respect to the Company that would have retroactive effect to any Pre-Closing Tax Period, (ii) amend any Tax Return of the Company for any Pre-Closing Tax Period, or (iii) initiate any voluntary disclosure or similar proceeding with any Governmental Authority with respect to any Pre-Closing Tax Period.
596: 
597: **Section 6.08 Employee Matters**
598: 
599: **(a)** For a period of not less than twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, provide each employee of the Company who continues in employment with the Company following the Closing (each, a \"Continuing Employee\") with (i) base salary or wages at least equal to the base salary or wages provided to such Continuing Employee immediately prior to the Closing, and (ii) employee benefits that are, in the aggregate, substantially comparable to those provided to such Continuing Employee immediately prior to the Closing. Nothing in this Section 6.08 shall be construed to guarantee employment for any specific period of time, to restrict Buyer\'s or the Company\'s right to terminate the employment of any employee, or to create any third-party beneficiary rights in favor of any employee.
600: 
601: **(b)** With respect to any Employee Benefit Plan maintained by Buyer or the Company following the Closing, Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, credit each Continuing Employee with his or her years of service with the Company (and any predecessor entities) prior to the Closing Date for purposes of eligibility to participate, vesting, and benefit accrual (but not for purposes of benefit accrual under any defined benefit pension plan).
602: 
603: **(c)** Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, permit each Continuing Employee who participates in the Company\'s 401(k) plan to roll over his or her account balance under such plan into a tax-qualified defined contribution plan maintained by Buyer or the Company following the Closing, in accordance with applicable Law.
604: 
605: **Section 6.09 Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation**
606: 
607: **(a)** *Non-Competition.* For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States; *provided* that the foregoing shall not restrict Seller or its Affiliates from (i) owning, directly or indirectly, solely as a passive investment, securities of any Person that are traded on a national securities exchange if Seller and its Affiliates do not, directly or indirectly, beneficially own five percent (5%) or more of any class of securities of such Person, or (ii) performing its obligations under this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents.
