Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither Seller nor the Company shall be required to pay or commit to pay any amount to (or incur any obligation in favor of) any Person from whom any such consent or waiver may be required (other than filing, application, or similar fees imposed by any Governmental Authority).
**Section 6.06 Public Announcements**

Neither Party shall, and each Party shall cause its respective Affiliates not to, issue any press release or make any public announcement relating to the subject matter of this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed); *provided* that either Party may make any public disclosure that it believes in good faith is required by applicable Law, any listing or trading agreement concerning its publicly traded securities, or any rule or regulation of any securities exchange or self-regulatory organization, in which case the disclosing Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to advise the other Party prior to making the disclosure and to provide the other Party with a reasonable opportunity to review and comment upon such disclosure.
**Section 6.07 Tax Matters**

**(a)** *Pre-Closing Tax Returns.* Seller shall prepare and timely file (or cause to be prepared and timely filed) all Tax Returns of the Company for any Pre-Closing Tax Period that are due (taking into account any valid extensions) after the Closing Date. All such Tax Returns shall be prepared in a manner consistent with past practice (unless otherwise required by applicable Law). Seller shall provide drafts of such Tax Returns to Buyer for its review and comment at least thirty (30) days prior to the due date for filing (or, if such Tax Return is due less than forty-five (45) days after the Closing Date, as soon as reasonably practicable). Seller shall consider in good faith any reasonable comments provided by Buyer. Seller shall timely pay or cause to be paid all Taxes shown as due and payable on such Tax Returns.

**(b)** *Straddle Period Tax Returns.* For any taxable period that includes, but does not end on, the Closing Date (each, a \"Straddle Period\"), the Taxes of the Company attributable to the portion of such Straddle Period ending on and including the Closing Date (the \"Pre-Closing Straddle Amount\") shall be determined using a \"closing-of-the-books\" methodology as of the end of the Closing Date, except that Taxes imposed on a periodic basis (such as real property Taxes) shall be allocated to the Pre-Closing Straddle Amount based on the number of days in the Straddle Period falling on or before the Closing Date relative to the total number of days in such Straddle Period.

**(c)** *Transfer Taxes.* All transfer, documentary, sales, use, stamp, registration, value-added, and other similar Taxes and fees (including any penalties and interest) imposed in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (collectively, \"Transfer Taxes\") shall be borne equally by Buyer and Seller. The Party required by applicable Law to file the Tax Return with respect to any Transfer Tax shall file such Tax Return in a timely manner, and the other Party shall promptly reimburse such filing Party for its allocable share of such Transfer Tax.

**(d)** *Cooperation.* After the Closing, Buyer and Seller shall cooperate fully, as and to the extent reasonably requested by the other Party, in connection with the filing of Tax Returns of the Company and the conduct of any audit, litigation, or other proceeding with respect to Taxes of the Company. Such cooperation shall include the retention and, upon the other Party\'s request, the provision of records and information that are reasonably relevant to any such Tax Return, audit, litigation, or other proceeding, and making employees available on a mutually convenient basis to provide additional information and explanation of any material provided hereunder.

**(e)** *Tax Elections.* Neither Buyer nor the Company shall, without the prior written consent of Seller (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), (i) make or change any Tax election with respect to the Company that would have retroactive effect to any Pre-Closing Tax Period, (ii) amend any Tax Return of the Company for any Pre-Closing Tax Period, or (iii) initiate any voluntary disclosure or similar proceeding with any Governmental Authority with respect to any Pre-Closing Tax Period.
**Section 6.08 Employee Matters**

**(a)** For a period of not less than twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, provide each employee of the Company who continues in employment with the Company following the Closing (each, a \"Continuing Employee\") with (i) base salary or wages at least equal to the base salary or wages provided to such Continuing Employee immediately prior to the Closing, and (ii) employee benefits that are, in the aggregate, substantially comparable to those provided to such Continuing Employee immediately prior to the Closing. Nothing in this Section 6.08 shall be construed to guarantee employment for any specific period of time, to restrict Buyer\'s or the Company\'s right to terminate the employment of any employee, or to create any third-party beneficiary rights in favor of any employee.

**(b)** With respect to any Employee Benefit Plan maintained by Buyer or the Company following the Closing, Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, credit each Continuing Employee with his or her years of service with the Company (and any predecessor entities) prior to the Closing Date for purposes of eligibility to participate, vesting, and benefit accrual (but not for purposes of benefit accrual under any defined benefit pension plan).

**(c)** Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, permit each Continuing Employee who participates in the Company\'s 401(k) plan to roll over his or her account balance under such plan into a tax-qualified defined contribution plan maintained by Buyer or the Company following the Closing, in accordance with applicable Law.
**Section 6.09 Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation**

**(a)** *Non-Competition.* For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States; *provided* that the foregoing shall not restrict Seller or its Affiliates from (i) owning, directly or indirectly, solely as a passive investment, securities of any Person that are traded on a national securities exchange if Seller and its Affiliates do not, directly or indirectly, beneficially own five percent (5%) or more of any class of securities of such Person, or (ii) performing its obligations under this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents.

**(b)** *Non-Solicitation.* For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, (i) solicit, recruit, hire, or engage (or attempt to solicit, recruit, hire, or engage) any employee of the Company, or (ii) solicit or encourage (or attempt to solicit or encourage) any customer, supplier, licensee, licensor, or other business relationship of the Company to cease or reduce its business with the Company; *provided* that the foregoing shall not restrict (A) general solicitations of employment not specifically directed toward employees of the Company, including through advertisements in newspapers, trade journals, or online job boards, or (B) solicitations by headhunters or recruiting firms not specifically directed by Seller or its Affiliates to target employees of the Company.

**(c)** *Remedies.* The Parties acknowledge and agree that a breach of any of the restrictive covenants set forth in this Section 6.09 would cause irreparable damage to Buyer and the Company and that monetary damages alone would not provide an adequate remedy. Accordingly, in the event of any actual or threatened breach by Seller or any of its Affiliates of the provisions of this Section 6.09, Buyer and the Company shall be entitled to seek specific performance and injunctive relief (temporary, preliminary, and permanent) from any court of competent jurisdiction, without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity. The restrictive covenants contained in this Section 6.09 are independent of any other provision of this Agreement, and the existence of any claim or cause of action of Seller against Buyer, whether predicated on this Agreement or otherwise, shall not constitute a defense to the enforcement of such restrictive covenants.
**Section 6.10 Directors\' and Officers\' Insurance**

For a period of six (6) years following the Closing Date, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain in effect directors\' and officers\' liability insurance (\"D&O Tail Insurance\") covering acts or omissions occurring at or prior to the Closing Date with respect to those Persons who are or were directors or officers of the Company at or prior to the Closing Date, on terms (including coverage amounts, retentions, and other material terms) that are no less favorable in the aggregate than the D&O insurance maintained by the Company as of the date of this Agreement; *provided* that the annual premium for such D&O Tail Insurance shall not exceed 250% of the annual premium currently paid by the Company for its existing D&O insurance.
**Section 6.11 Further Assurances**

From time to time following the Closing, each Party shall, and shall cause its Affiliates to, execute and deliver such additional documents, instruments, conveyances, and assurances, and take such further actions as may be reasonably required to carry out the provisions of this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents and to give effect to the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby.
**[ARTICLE VII]{.underline}**
**[CONDITIONS TO CLOSING]{.underline}**
**Section 7.01 Conditions to Each Party\'s Obligations**

The respective obligations of each Party to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or, to the extent permitted by applicable Law, waiver by each Party) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** No Governmental Authority shall have enacted, issued, promulgated, enforced, or entered any Law, order, injunction, judgment, decree, ruling, or other legally binding action (whether temporary, preliminary, or permanent) that is then in effect and that has the effect of making the transactions contemplated by this Agreement illegal or otherwise preventing or prohibiting the consummation of such transactions.
**(b)** The applicable waiting period (and any extension thereof) under the HSR Act in respect of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall have expired or been terminated.

**(c)** No Action by any Governmental Authority shall be pending that seeks to (i) restrain, enjoin, prevent, prohibit, or make illegal the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, (ii) impose limitations on the ability of Buyer to effectively exercise full rights of ownership of the Shares, or (iii) compel Buyer or any of its Affiliates to dispose of or hold separate all or a material portion of the business or assets of the Company.
**Section 7.02 Conditions to Buyer\'s Obligations**

The obligations of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by Buyer) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** *Representations and Warranties.* (i) The Fundamental Representations of Seller shall be true and correct in all respects (other than de minimis inaccuracies) as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date, in which case such representation or warranty shall be true and correct as of such earlier date); and (ii) each other representation and warranty of Seller and the Company contained in this Agreement (without giving effect to any qualification as to \"materiality\" or \"Material Adverse Effect\" contained therein) shall be true and correct as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date), except, in the case of this clause (ii), where the failure of such representations and warranties to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.

**(b)** *Covenants.* Seller shall have performed and complied in all material respects with all covenants and agreements required to be performed or complied with by Seller under this Agreement at or prior to the Closing.

**(c)** *No Material Adverse Effect.* Since the date of this Agreement, no event, change, effect, development, condition, or occurrence shall have occurred that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.

**(d)** *Officer\'s Certificate.* Seller shall have delivered to Buyer a certificate, signed by a duly authorized officer of Seller, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Sections 7.02(a), 7.02(b), and 7.02(c) have been satisfied.
**(e)** *Seller Deliverables.* Seller shall have delivered to Buyer all of the closing deliverables set forth in Section 2.08(a).
**(f)** *Third-Party Consents.* All consents, waivers, approvals, and authorizations set forth on Schedule 4.05 shall have been obtained and shall be in full force and effect.
**(g)** *Escrow Agreement.* The Escrow Agreement shall have been duly executed and delivered by Seller and the Escrow Agent.
**Section 7.03 Conditions to Seller\'s Obligations**

The obligations of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by Seller) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** *Representations and Warranties.* Each representation and warranty of Buyer contained in this Agreement (without giving effect to any qualification as to \"materiality\" contained therein) shall be true and correct as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date), except where the failure of such representations and warranties to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to prevent or materially delay the ability of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

**(b)** *Covenants.* Buyer shall have performed and complied in all material respects with all covenants and agreements required to be performed or complied with by Buyer under this Agreement at or prior to the Closing.
**(c)** *Closing Payments.* Buyer shall have delivered the Closing Payment to Seller and the Escrow Amount to the Escrow Agent in accordance with Section 2.03.

**(d)** *Officer\'s Certificate.* Buyer shall have delivered to Seller a certificate, signed by a duly authorized officer or manager of Buyer, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Sections 7.03(a) and 7.03(b) have been satisfied.
**(e)** *Buyer Deliverables.* Buyer shall have delivered to Seller all of the closing deliverables set forth in Section 2.08(b).
**[ARTICLE VIII]{.underline}**
**[TERMINATION]{.underline}**
**Section 8.01 Termination**
This Agreement may be terminated at any time prior to the Closing:
**(a)** by the mutual written consent of Buyer and Seller;

**(b)** by either Buyer or Seller, by written notice to the other Party, if the Closing shall not have occurred on or before the Outside Date (February 28, 2026); *provided* that the right to terminate this Agreement under this Section 8.01(b) shall not be available to any Party whose breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement set forth in this Agreement has been the primary cause of, or has primarily resulted in, the failure of the Closing to occur on or before the Outside Date;

**(c)** by either Buyer or Seller, by written notice to the other Party, if any Governmental Authority shall have enacted, issued, promulgated, enforced, or entered any final and non-appealable Law, order, injunction, judgment, decree, ruling, or other legally binding action that permanently restrains, enjoins, or otherwise prohibits the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement;

**(d)** by Buyer, by written notice to Seller, if there shall have been a breach by Seller of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement that would cause the conditions set forth in Section 7.02(a) or Section 7.02(b) not to be satisfied, and such breach shall not have been cured by Seller within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice of such breach from Buyer (or, if earlier, by the Outside Date); *provided* that Buyer shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement under this Section 8.01(d) if Buyer is then in material breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement; or

**(e)** by Seller, by written notice to Buyer, if there shall have been a breach by Buyer of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement that would cause the conditions set forth in Section 7.03(a) or Section 7.03(b) not to be satisfied, and such breach shall not have been cured by Buyer within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice of such breach from Seller (or, if earlier, by the Outside Date); *provided* that Seller shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement under this Section 8.01(e) if Seller is then in material breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement.
**Section 8.02 Effect of Termination**

In the event of the termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 8.01, this Agreement shall forthwith become void and have no effect, without any liability on the part of any Party or its respective Affiliates, directors, officers, employees, stockholders, members, managers, partners, agents, or Representatives, and all rights and obligations of the Parties hereunder shall cease; *provided*, *however*, that (a) nothing herein shall relieve any Party from liability for any willful and material breach of this Agreement occurring prior to such termination or for fraud; and (b) the provisions of Section 6.03 (Confidentiality), Section 6.06 (Public Announcements), Section 8.02 (Effect of Termination), Section 8.03 (Expenses), and Article X (Miscellaneous) shall survive any termination of this Agreement and shall remain in full force and effect.
**Section 8.03 Expenses**

Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement (including with respect to HSR Act filing fees, which shall be paid by Buyer pursuant to Section 6.04(c), and Transfer Taxes, which shall be allocated pursuant to Section 6.07(c)), all costs, fees, and expenses (including attorneys\' fees, accountants\' fees, financial advisory fees, and other professional fees and expenses) incurred by or on behalf of a Party in connection with this Agreement and the transactions contemplated hereby shall be paid by the Party incurring such costs, fees, and expenses, whether or not the transactions contemplated by this Agreement are consummated.
**[ARTICLE IX]{.underline}**
**[INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**
**Section 9.01 Survival**

**(a)** The Fundamental Representations shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect until the date that is sixty (60) days following the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations relating to the matters covered thereby (giving effect to any waiver, mitigation, or extension thereof).

**(b)** All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire and be of no further force or effect.

**(c)** All covenants and agreements of the Parties contained in this Agreement that by their terms are to be performed in whole or in part after the Closing shall survive the Closing in accordance with their terms. All covenants and agreements of the Parties that are to be performed in whole prior to or at the Closing shall survive the Closing for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date.

**(d)** No claim for indemnification under this Article IX may be asserted by any Buyer Indemnitee or Seller Indemnitee after the expiration of the applicable survival period set forth in this Section 9.01; *provided* that any claim for indemnification that is properly asserted in writing in accordance with Section 9.05 prior to the expiration of the applicable survival period shall survive such expiration until such claim has been finally resolved.

{"file_path":"spa-markup-memorandum.md","content":"# PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

## SPA MARKUP MEMORANDUM

**Project Cascade — Acquisition of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.**  
**To:** Elena Vasquez-Moreno, Partner, M&A Group; Jonathan Kreider, Senior Associate, M&A Group  
**From:** Deal Team — Buyer-Side SPA Review  
**Date:** October 29, 2025  
**Re:** Buyer markup of Seller’s draft Stock Purchase Agreement circulated October 22, 2025

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Seller’s draft is materially seller-favorable and departs from the executed September 10, 2025 binding term sheet on several binding economic and risk-allocation terms. The markup should be delivered as a focused buyer redline, not a general rewrite. The most important corrections are:

1. **MAE definition (Critical):** add a disproportionate-impact qualifier to the environmental-services-industry and Environmental Laws carve-outs.
2. **Pro-sandbagging (Critical):** delete Section 9.06’s anti-sandbagging provision and replace it with an affirmative pro-sandbagging clause.
3. **Special Indemnity (Critical):** add a separate Dalton Creek CERCLA Special Indemnity, with 72-month survival, dollar-one recovery, no general basket or cap, and 36-month escrow support.
4. **Government contracts (Critical):** add specific FAR 42.12 / Anti-Assignment Act and state-government-contract novation provisions, including pre-closing submissions, representations, a balanced closing condition, and a post-closing cooperation tail.
5. **Earnout operations and mechanics (Critical/High):** strike the affirmative “past practice / maximize” covenant, preserve Buyer’s operational flexibility, and conform timing and Adjusted EBITDA mechanics to the term sheet and playbook.
6. **Indemnification cap (Critical):** replace the Seller’s $43,000,000 / 20% cap with the binding $26,875,000 / 12.5% cap.
7. **Environmental survival (High):** extend Section 4.15 environmental representations to 36 months, while preserving the option to seek the full applicable statute-of-limitations period; also restore the term-sheet 18-month general survival period.
8. **Affiliate transactions, payoff mechanics, permits, R&W insurance, and non-compete (High/Medium):** add the missing interim affiliate-transaction restriction; require payoff letters at least three Business Days before Closing and simultaneous payoff; add permit notification/transfer covenants; add the R&W insurer subrogation waiver; and conform the non-compete to the term sheet.

### Deal facts driving the markup

- **Base Enterprise Value:** $215,000,000.
- **Binding general cap:** 12.5% of Base Enterprise Value = **$26,875,000**.
- **Binding basket:** 1.0% of Base Enterprise Value = **$2,150,000**, true deductible. This is within the playbook range and should not be marked up.
- **Escrow:** $16,125,000 (7.5% of Base Enterprise Value) with Pinnacle Trust Company; general release at 18 months; Fundamental Representation and Special Indemnity holdback at 36 months.
- **Dalton Creek:** EPA CERCLA § 104(e) information request; estimated exposure **$1,500,000–$6,000,000**; known environmental risk requiring a separate Special Indemnity.
- **Hargrove:** active Oregon DEQ remediation; approximately **$4,200,000** of remaining cost; project-specific policy limit of **$10,000,000**.
- **Permits:** 23 active permits across Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada; change-of-control notices or approvals may be required.
- **Government contracts:** four active contracts with approximate annual value of $31.6 million in the aggregate; federal contracts require FAR 42.12 analysis and likely novation/recognition submissions.
- **Employees:** approximately 340 full-time employees; 12 PE-licensed employees are important to permit compliance.

### Recommended negotiation posture

The Critical items should be presented as corrections to binding deal terms or required risk allocation, not as opening positions. For government contracts, the recommended position is a balanced condition requiring submission of all required requests and no denial or threatened termination before Closing, rather than a hard condition requiring completed novations. The environmental representation survival should be marked at 36 months now, with authority reserved to seek the full applicable limitations period if the client elects that position after the October 27 call.

---

## 2. Source documents and review conventions

This memorandum cross-references:

- **Seller’s draft SPA** — `sellers-draft-spa.docx`, circulated October 22, 2025.
- **Executed Binding Term Sheet** — `executed-term-sheet.docx`, dated September 10, 2025.
- **Buyer M&A Playbook** — `buyer-ma-playbook.docx`, Version 4.2 (October 2025).
- **Environmental DD Memo** — `environmental-dd-memo.docx`, dated October 18, 2025.
- **Partner markup instructions** — email from Elena Vasquez-Moreno dated October 23, 2025.

For each issue below, “Seller draft” quotes the operative language to be deleted or revised. “Buyer replacement” is complete contract language intended for insertion into the SPA. The “Track-changes comment” is the margin-comment text to accompany the redline and identifies the supporting source.

---

# 3. Article I — Definitions

## 3.1 Material Adverse Effect — disproportionate-impact qualifiers

**Priority: Critical**

### Seller draft

Section 1.01 defines “Material Adverse Effect” and excludes:

> “(ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry;”
>
> “(iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations;”

The draft contains no exception for disproportionate effects on the Company.

### Buyer replacement language

Replace clauses (ii) and (iii) of the definition of “Material Adverse Effect” with the following:

> **(ii)** changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry, **except to the extent such changes disproportionately affect the Company relative to other participants in the environmental services industry**;
>
> **(iii)** changes in Environmental Laws or regulations, **except to the extent such changes disproportionately affect the Company relative to other participants in the environmental services industry**;

All other portions of the definition remain unchanged.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The environmental-services and regulatory carve-outs cannot be absolute in this transaction. Cascadia’s value is directly tied to environmental regulation and environmental-services demand; an industry-wide or regulatory change that disproportionately harms Cascadia must remain available to support the MAE closing condition. This correction is required by **Playbook § 2.1** and the partner’s October 23 instructions. It also protects the buyer from precisely the sector-specific risks identified in the **DD Memo §§ I and V**.

---

## 3.2 Indemnification Cap definition

**Priority: Critical**

### Seller draft

> “**Indemnification Cap**” means Forty-Three Million Dollars ($43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.

### Buyer replacement language

> “**Indemnification Cap**” means **Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars ($26,875,000), which is equal to twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value**.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The Seller draft changes a binding economic term. Section 8 of the executed Term Sheet fixes the general cap at 12.5% of the $215,000,000 Base Enterprise Value, or $26,875,000. The 20% / $43,000,000 figure is not a negotiated alternative; it is a direct deviation from the binding term sheet. See **Term Sheet § 8** and **Playbook §§ 5.1 and 14 (Checklist Item 3)**.

---

# 4. Article II — Purchase price, earnout, and closing mechanics

## 4.1 Earnout covenant — eliminate affirmative operating obligations

**Priority: Critical**

### Seller draft

Section 2.05(d) provides:

> “From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. Without limiting the foregoing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action that would reasonably be expected to reduce the Adjusted EBITDA of the Company below the levels that would otherwise have been achieved. In furtherance of the foregoing, during the Earnout Period, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources as in effect immediately prior to the Closing Date and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates.”

### Buyer replacement language

Delete Section 2.05(d) in its entirety and replace it with:

> **(d) Operation of the Business During the Earnout Period.** Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action **with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment**. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05(d) shall restrict Buyer’s right to operate, integrate, restructure, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer’s sole discretion, including the right to make capital expenditure decisions, change pricing, make personnel decisions, make strategic investments, acquire or dispose of businesses or assets, enter new markets, discontinue or modify product or service lines, allocate corporate overhead, combine the Company with Buyer or any Affiliate, or make other operational modifications. No such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05(d) unless taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. Buyer shall have no obligation to maintain the Company as a separate entity, maintain any particular level of personnel, equipment, or capital expenditures, retain any particular employee, refrain from diverting or redirecting any contract, customer, revenue, or business opportunity, or operate the Company in a manner consistent with past practice.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The Seller’s language would restrict integration, restructuring, personnel, capital allocation, pricing, and strategic decisions throughout the earnout period and would create litigation over ordinary post-closing business judgment. The executed Term Sheet expressly requires only a negative covenant against actions taken with the **primary purpose** of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. The replacement tracks **Term Sheet § 5 (Earnout Covenant)** and **Playbook § 7.2**. It is also consistent with the firm’s PE-buyer position that the buyer does not owe an affirmative duty to maximize an earnout.

---

## 4.2 Earnout financial mechanics and Adjusted EBITDA

**Priority: High**

### Seller draft

The draft provides:

> “Adjusted EBITDA” means net income determined under GAAP applied consistently with past practice, plus interest, taxes, and depreciation and amortization, and further adjusted to exclude “(i) non-recurring transaction costs,” “(ii) purchase-price accounting adjustments,” “(iii) extraordinary or non-recurring items,” and “(iv) any management fees, monitoring fees, or similar fees charged by Buyer or any of its Affiliates.”

Section 2.05(c) provides that Buyer delivers the Earnout Statement **within sixty (60) days** after the end of the Earnout Period. Section 2.05(e) provides that payment is due **within ten (10) Business Days after final determination**.

### Buyer replacement language

Replace the definition of “Adjusted EBITDA” with:

> “**Adjusted EBITDA**” means, for any period, the net income of the Company for such period, determined in accordance with GAAP applied consistently with the Company’s past practice, plus (a) interest expense, (b) income tax expense, and (c) depreciation and amortization expense, in each case to the extent deducted in determining net income, and further adjusted to exclude or add back, without duplication: (i) transaction-related costs and expenses incurred in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including legal, accounting, advisory, financing, diligence, and other professional fees; (ii) purchase-price accounting adjustments arising from the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby; (iii) Buyer-directed integration costs, restructuring charges, and other post-Closing costs incurred in connection with integrating or restructuring the Company; (iv) extraordinary, non-recurring, or one-time items, including one-time litigation costs, regulatory penalties, and other extraordinary items; (v) management fees, monitoring fees, corporate overhead allocations, or other charges imposed by Buyer or any of its Affiliates that were not charged to the Company on a consistent basis before the Closing; (vi) intercompany charges from Buyer or its Affiliates that are not attributable to goods or services provided to the Company on arm’s-length terms and consistent with pre-Closing practice; (vii) the portion of rent, compensation, or other expenses attributable to related-party arrangements that are not on arm’s-length terms, including any above-market portion of the Affiliate Lease; and (viii) such other items expressly identified on Exhibit D. Adjusted EBITDA shall not be adjusted to give effect to purchase-price accounting or Buyer financing decisions, except as expressly provided in this definition or Exhibit D.

Replace Section 2.05(c) with:

> **(c) Earnout Calculation and Dispute Resolution.** Within **forty-five (45) days** after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the “Earnout Statement”) setting forth Buyer’s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period, together with reasonable supporting detail. Seller shall have thirty (30) days after receipt to review the Earnout Statement and deliver a written objection specifying each disputed item and the amount Seller believes is correct. > **(b) Final Release.** With respect to any portion of the Escrow Fund retained as a Pending Claims Reserve, such amounts shall continue to be held in the Escrow Fund until (i) final resolution of the applicable pending claim in accordance with this Article IX or (ii) the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date with respect to claims relating to Fundamental Representations or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. Upon final resolution of each pending claim, the Escrow Agent shall promptly release (A) to Buyer, the amount of Losses finally determined to be payable to Buyer Indemnitees with respect to such claim, and (B) to Seller, the excess, if any, of the Pending Claims Reserve attributable to such claim over the amount released to Buyer. For the avoidance of doubt, release of the Escrow Fund at 36 months shall not terminate or limit Buyer’s right to pursue the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity directly against Seller through the 72-month survival period.

Replace Exhibit A clause (c) with:

> **(c)** the release of amounts from the Escrow Fund in accordance with Section 9.08, including an eighteen (18)-month general release and a thirty-six (36)-month holdback for amounts subject to pending claims relating to Fundamental Representations or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, without limiting Buyer’s right to pursue any such claim directly against Seller after release of the Escrow Fund.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The $16,125,000 escrow and 18-/36-month release structure are agreed terms, but the draft omits the Special Indemnity from the 36-month holdback. The term sheet and **DD Memo § III.C** require escrow support for the Dalton Creek matter for at least 36 months; the Special Indemnity itself must survive 72 months. See **Term Sheet §§ 4 and 9** and **Playbook § 5.4**.

---

## 8.6 Pro-sandbagging; delete Section 9.06

**Priority: Critical**

### Seller draft

Section 9.06 provides:

> “Buyer shall not be entitled to indemnification under this Article IX with respect to any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty of Seller or the Company of which Buyer or any of its Representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.”

### Buyer replacement language

Delete Section 9.06 in its entirety and replace it with:

> **Section 9.06 Effect of Investigation and Knowledge.** The right of Buyer and the other Buyer Indemnitees to indemnification or any other remedy based on the representations, warranties, covenants, and obligations set forth in this Agreement shall not be affected, limited, diminished, or otherwise impaired by any investigation conducted by or on behalf of Buyer or any of its Affiliates or Representatives, or by any knowledge acquired or capable of being acquired by Buyer or any of its Affiliates or Representatives, at any time before or after the execution and delivery of this Agreement or the Closing Date, with respect to the accuracy or inaccuracy of, or compliance with, any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation. No claim for indemnification shall be defeated or reduced by reason of any investigation, knowledge, notice, or other information of Buyer or any of its Affiliates or Representatives, whether obtained before or after the Closing.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The existing provision is an express anti-sandbagging clause and is unacceptable. It would penalize Buyer for conducting the extensive financial, legal, environmental, regulatory, and operational diligence reflected in the **DD Memo**, including diligence that identified the Dalton Creek matter. The replacement is required by **Playbook § 5.3 and Checklist Item 5**, the partner’s October 23 instructions, and the buyer’s agreed risk-allocation position. The representations remain contractual risk allocation even where Buyer has discovered facts during diligence.

---

## 8.7 R&W insurance subrogation waiver

**Priority: Medium**

### Seller draft

The Seller draft contains no R&W insurance subrogation waiver. It does not address Granite Ridge Underwriters or any R&W policy.

### Buyer replacement language

Add the following as new Section 9.10:

> **Section 9.10 R&W Insurance; Subrogation Waiver.** If Buyer or any of its Affiliates obtains a representations and warranties insurance policy in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cause the insurer, in the policy or a related written waiver, to waive any right of subrogation, contribution, recourse, or other claim against Seller, its Affiliates, and their respective directors, officers, employees, agents, Representatives, and equityholders in respect of any claim paid under that policy, **except with respect to actual fraud by Seller**. Buyer shall not amend or waive this protection in a manner that would expand the insurer’s rights against Seller, except with Seller’s prior written consent. Nothing in this Section 9.10 shall limit Seller’s direct obligations under this Agreement, including the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The Term Sheet § 10 and **Playbook § 8.2** require a waiver of R&W insurer subrogation against Seller except for actual fraud. The R&W policy supplements, and does not replace or reduce, the SPA’s agreed indemnification structure, particularly for known environmental liabilities that may be excluded or sub-limited by the policy. The identified carrier is Granite Ridge Underwriters.

---

# 9. Article VI — Non-Competition and Non-Solicitation

## 9.1 Conform non-compete and non-solicit to the term sheet

**Priority: Medium**

### Seller draft

Section 6.09 provides:

> “For a period of five (5) years … Seller shall not … engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States ….”

It also imposes a three-year non-solicitation covering Company employees, customers, suppliers, licensees, licensors, and other business relationships.

### Buyer replacement language

Replace Section 6.09(a) and (b) with:

> **(a) Non-Competition.** For a period of **three (3) years** following the Closing Date, Seller and its controlled Affiliates shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, or control of any business engaged in the provision of **environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services**, as those services are conducted by the Company as of the Closing Date, in **Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada**. For the avoidance of doubt, this covenant shall not apply to any portfolio company or operating subsidiary of Seller that is not engaged in environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services as of the Closing Date.
>
> The foregoing shall not restrict Seller or its Affiliates from (i) conducting their existing construction and timber operations as conducted as of the Closing Date; (ii) holding, solely as a passive investment, less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of any publicly traded entity; or (iii) performing environmental-related activities that are incidental to and performed solely in connection with Seller’s construction or timber operations, including erosion control, stormwater management, and environmental compliance activities at Seller’s own sites.
>
> **(b) Non-Solicitation.** For a period of **two (2) years** following the Closing Date, Seller and its Affiliates shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any individual who is an employee of the Company as of the Closing Date, or induce, encourage, or attempt to induce or encourage any such employee to terminate employment with the Company; provided that this Section 6.09(b) shall not restrict (i) general solicitations of employment that are not specifically directed at or targeted toward Company employees, including advertisements, job postings, or use of recruiting firms, or (ii) the hiring of any Company employee who contacts Seller or its Affiliates on the employee’s own initiative without solicitation by or on behalf of Seller or its Affiliates.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The Seller draft is materially broader than the binding term sheet: five years versus three; all U.S. businesses versus environmental remediation and hazardous waste management; nationwide versus four states; and three-year customer/supplier restrictions that are not in the agreed term sheet. The replacement tracks **Term Sheet § 11**, including the construction/timber carve-outs that prevent the covenant from capturing Seller’s unrelated operations. See **Playbook § 10.1 and Checklist Item 10**. The covenant should be reviewed under the governing state-law enforceability rules before final execution.

---

# 10. Additional diligence-driven markup and observations

## 10.1 Hargrove remediation and environmental insurance maintenance

**Priority: High**

### Seller draft

Section 6.01(a)(iii) generally requires the Company to maintain insurance, and Section 4.15(f) identifies the two environmental policies. The draft does not expressly require continuity of the Hargrove site-specific policy or address the $4,200,000 remaining remediation obligation.

### Buyer replacement language

Add the following to Section 6.01(a) as new clause (v):

> **(v)** maintain in full force and effect, without cancellation, lapse, material reduction, or material modification, each environmental insurance policy identified in Section 4.15(f), including Environmental Impairment Liability Policy No. EIL-2024-08821 and Project-Specific Environmental Liability Policy No. PSE-2023-04417, and timely pay all premiums and other amounts due under such policies.

Add the following to Section 4.15(d) or, alternatively, to Schedule 4.15(d):

> The Hargrove Industrial Site remediation project at 3200 SE Industrial Way, Milwaukie, Oregon, is being performed under Oregon DEQ Contract No. DEQ-OR-2022-0847, Task Order No. 14. The estimated remaining cost to complete the project is approximately $4,200,000 over the next 24 to 36 months. The Company has disclosed all material work plans, schedules, notices, claims, cost estimates, and communications with Oregon DEQ relating to the project. No material default, notice of violation, stop-work order, or threatened termination has been received, and Policy No. PSE-2023-04417 remains in force with a $10,000,000 policy limit.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The **DD Memo §§ IV.A–C and VII** identifies Hargrove as a moderate risk with $4.2 million of remaining costs, potential regulatory and third-party claims, and insurance that appears adequate but remains subject to exclusions and coverage defenses. The SPA should preserve the coverage and accurately state the project status. This is separate from, and does not replace, the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity.

## 10.2 PE-licensed personnel

**Priority: Medium**

### Seller draft

Section 4.14(c) states that 12 employees hold PE licenses and, to Company Knowledge, the licenses are in good standing. It does not address whether the Company has received notice that any such employee intends to resign or whether the Company has a continuity plan for permit-critical personnel.

### Buyer replacement language

Replace Section 4.14(c) with:

> **(c) Professional Licenses.** Schedule 4.14(b) sets forth a true and complete list of the twelve (12) employees of the Company who hold professional engineer licenses, including each name, license number, and state of licensure. All such licenses are current and in good standing, and no Action is pending or, to Seller’s Knowledge, threatened to revoke, suspend, limit, or condition any such license. The Company has not received written notice from any such employee of an intention to resign, terminate employment, or cease performing the functions for which the employee’s license is required, and no such employee has notified the Company of an intention not to continue in employment following the Closing.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** Twelve PE-licensed employees are identified as critical to permit compliance in **DD Memo § V.A**. The proposed language is a targeted representation, not a guarantee of continued employment. Buyer should separately consider retention or employment arrangements for permit-critical personnel.

## 10.3 Disclosure schedule factual cleanup

**Priority: Medium**

The following inconsistencies should be corrected or confirmed before the buyer redline is finalized:

- **Dalton Creek location:** Seller Schedule 4.15(d) says Lane County; the DD Memo and Term Sheet say Clackamas County.
- **EPA request date:** DD Memo says February 12, 2025; Seller Schedule 4.15(d) says June 12, 2025.
- **EIL policy number:** Seller SPA Schedule 4.17 and the DD Memo identify EIL-2024-08821; the Term Sheet background paragraph lists EIL-2024-0093712.
- **Outside counsel:** DD Memo identifies Brannick & Associates; the Term Sheet background paragraph identifies Haverford Environmental Law Group.
- **Buyer fund / financing references:** SPA § 5.04 refers to a debt commitment letter dated “[●], 2025” and an equity commitment from Whitmore Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P.; the executed Term Sheet identifies a September 3, 2025 Clearwater commitment and describes the acquisition as a Fund III platform investment. Confirm and conform the SPA to the actual financing documents and fund entity.
- **Confidentiality agreement date:** SPA § 6.03 says June 20, 2025; the Term Sheet § 17 refers to a July 12, 2025 confidentiality agreement. Confirm the operative agreement and date.

These items should be corrected through schedules and defined-term cleanup, not silently left to create ambiguity in the indemnity or closing conditions.

---

# 11. Items not to mark up

The following provisions are within the buyer’s accepted range and should remain unchanged absent partner or client instruction:

1. **Basket:** $2,150,000, equal to 1.0% of Base Enterprise Value, and expressly structured as a true deductible. This is within **Playbook § 5.2** and matches **Term Sheet § 8**.
2. **Knowledge qualifier:** actual knowledge of Patricia Huang and Robert Merrill, without constructive knowledge. Cascadia has approximately 340 employees, so this is acceptable under **Playbook § 11.1**.
3. **Good-standing certificates:** certificates dated within ten Business Days of Closing are within the **Playbook § 11.2** 5–10 Business Day range and match **Term Sheet § 12**.
4. **Delaware governing law:** appropriate because Buyer and Seller are Delaware entities; do not mark up **SPA § 10.02** under **Playbook § 11.2**.
5. **Escrow amount:** $16,125,000, equal to 7.5% of Base Enterprise Value, is consistent with the executed Term Sheet. Mark up only the recovery and Special Indemnity mechanics, not the amount.
6. **Fundamental Representation survival:** statute of limitations plus 60 days is acceptable and consistent with the term sheet.

---

# 12. Consolidated priority list and negotiation notes

| Priority | SPA provision | Required action | Source / comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | MAE definition | Add disproportionate-impact qualifiers to industry and Environmental Laws carve-outs | Playbook § 2.1; partner email |
| Critical | § 9.06 | Delete anti-sandbagging; add pro-sandbagging | Playbook § 5.3; partner email |
| Critical | § 9.09 / new schedule | Add Dalton Creek Special Indemnity; 72 months; no basket/cap; 36-month escrow support | Term Sheet § 9; DD Memo §§ III, VIII |
| Critical | § 6.12 / § 7.02 | Add government contract novation/recognition covenants and balanced condition | DD Memo § VI; Playbook §§ 12.2, 13.2 |
| Critical | §§ 1.01, 9.04(b) | Replace $43 million / 20% cap with $26.875 million / 12.5% | Term Sheet § 8 |
| Critical | § 2.05(d) | Replace affirmative earnout operating obligations with primary-purpose negative covenant | Term Sheet § 5; Playbook § 7.2 |
| High | § 9.01(b) | Change general survival to 18 months; Environmental Representations to 36 months | Term Sheet § 8; Playbook § 4.2 |
| High | § 6.01(b) | Add affiliate transaction restriction | Playbook § 3.2; Schedule 4.21 |
| High | § 2.03(d), § 2.08, § 7.02 | Add payoff letters 3 Business Days before Closing; simultaneous payoff; condition | Term Sheet § 6; Playbook § 9.2 |
| High | § 6.13 / § 7.02 | Add environmental permit notification/transfer covenants and condition | DD Memo § V; Playbook § 12.1 |
| High | § 9.08 / Exhibit A | Hold Special Indemnity claims for 36 months; direct recovery remains available for 72 months | Term Sheet §§ 4, 9 |
| Medium | § 9.10 | Add R&W insurer subrogation waiver except fraud | Term Sheet § 10; Playbook § 8.2 |
| Medium | § 6.09 | Conform non-compete to 3 years / four states / defined business; non-solicit to 2 years and employees only | Term Sheet § 11; Playbook § 10.1 |
| Medium | §§ 4.14–4.17 | Tighten PE-license, environmental insurance, and schedule factual disclosures | DD Memo §§ IV, V, VII |

---

## 13. Closing recommendation

Deliver the markup with the Critical items presented as required corrections to the binding term sheet and core buyer risk allocation. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, pro-sandbagging clause, $26.875 million cap, MAE qualifiers, and earnout covenant should not be traded away without partner approval. The government contract and permit provisions should be framed as implementation of diligence-identified regulatory requirements. Before circulation, confirm the Dalton Creek county/date, EIL policy number, outside counsel, financing fund, and confidentiality agreement date against the source documents. 

The present redline position assumes: (i) 36-month environmental representation survival, with authority reserved to seek the full applicable limitations period; (ii) government-contract submission/no-denial as the closing condition, with a 12-month cooperation tail; and (iii) a portion of the existing escrow reserved for Dalton Creek claims for 36 months, without reducing the 72-month direct Special Indemnity.

**End of memorandum**

{"file_path":"spa-markup-memorandum.md","content":"# PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

## SPA MARKUP MEMORANDUM

**Project Cascade — Acquisition of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.**  
**To:** Elena Vasquez-Moreno, Partner, M&A Group; Jonathan Kreider, Senior Associate, M&A Group  
**From:** Deal Team — Buyer-Side SPA Review  
**Date:** October 29, 2025  
**Re:** Buyer markup of Seller’s draft Stock Purchase Agreement circulated October 22, 2025

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Seller’s draft is materially seller-favorable and departs from the executed September 10, 2025 binding term sheet on several binding economic and risk-allocation terms. The markup should be delivered as a focused buyer redline, not a general rewrite. The most important corrections are:

1. **MAE definition (Critical):** add a disproportionate-impact qualifier to the environmental-services-industry and Environmental Laws carve-outs.
2. **Pro-sandbagging (Critical):** delete Section 9.06’s anti-sandbagging provision and replace it with an affirmative pro-sandbagging clause.
3. **Special Indemnity (Critical):** add a separate Dalton Creek CERCLA Special Indemnity, with 72-month survival, dollar-one recovery, no general basket or cap, and 36-month escrow support.
4. **Government contracts (Critical):** add specific FAR 42.12 / Anti-Assignment Act and state-government-contract novation provisions, including pre-closing submissions, representations, a balanced closing condition, and a post-closing cooperation tail.
5. **Earnout operations and mechanics (Critical/High):** strike the affirmative “past practice / maximize” covenant, preserve Buyer’s operational flexibility, and conform timing and Adjusted EBITDA mechanics to the term sheet and playbook.
6. **Indemnification cap (Critical):** replace the Seller’s $43,000,000 / 20% cap with the binding $26,875,000 / 12.5% cap.
7. **Environmental survival (High):** extend Section 4.15 environmental representations to 36 months, while preserving the option to seek the full applicable statute-of-limitations period; also restore the term-sheet 18-month general survival period.
8. **Affiliate transactions, payoff mechanics, permits, R&W insurance, and non-compete (High/Medium):** add the missing interim affiliate-transaction restriction; require payoff letters at least three Business Days before Closing and simultaneous payoff; add permit notification/transfer covenants; add the R&W insurer subrogation waiver; and conform the non-compete to the term sheet.

### Deal facts driving the markup

- **Base Enterprise Value:** $215,000,000.
- **Binding general cap:** 12.5% of Base Enterprise Value = **$26,875,000**.
- **Binding basket:** 1.0% of Base Enterprise Value = **$2,150,000**, true deductible. This is within the playbook range and should not be marked up.
- **Escrow:** $16,125,000 (7.5% of Base Enterprise Value) with Pinnacle Trust Company; general release at 18 months; Fundamental Representation and Special Indemnity holdback at 36 months.
- **Dalton Creek:** EPA CERCLA § 104(e) information request; estimated exposure **$1,500,000–$6,000,000**; known environmental risk requiring a separate Special Indemnity.
- **Hargrove:** active Oregon DEQ remediation; approximately **$4,200,000** of remaining cost; project-specific policy limit of **$10,000,000**.
- **Permits:** 23 active permits across Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada; change-of-control notices or approvals may be required.
- **Government contracts:** four active contracts with approximate annual value of $31.6 million in the aggregate; federal contracts require FAR 42.12 analysis and likely novation/recognition submissions.
- **Employees:** approximately 340 full-time employees; 12 PE-licensed employees are important to permit compliance.

### Recommended negotiation posture

The Critical items should be presented as corrections to binding deal terms or required risk allocation, not as opening positions. For government contracts, the recommended position is a balanced condition requiring submission of all required requests and no denial or threatened termination before Closing, rather than a hard condition requiring completed novations. The environmental representation survival should be marked at 36 months now, with authority reserved to seek the full applicable limitations period if the client elects that position after the October 27 call.

---

## 2. Source documents and review conventions

This memorandum cross-references:

- **Seller’s draft SPA** — `sellers-draft-spa.docx`, circulated October 22, 2025.
- **Executed Binding Term Sheet** — `executed-term-sheet.docx`, dated September 10, 2025.
- **Buyer M&A Playbook** — `buyer-ma-playbook.docx`, Version 4.2 (October 2025).
- **Environmental DD Memo** — `environmental-dd-memo.docx`, dated October 18, 2025.
- **Partner markup instructions** — email from Elena Vasquez-Moreno dated October 23, 2025.

For each issue below, “Seller draft” quotes the operative language to be deleted or revised. “Buyer replacement” is complete contract language intended for insertion into the SPA. The “Track-changes comment” is the margin-comment text to accompany the redline and identifies the supporting source.

---

# 3. Article I — Definitions

## 3.1 Material Adverse Effect — disproportionate-impact qualifiers

**Priority: Critical**

### Seller draft

Section 1.01 defines “Material Adverse Effect” and excludes:

> “(ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry;”
>
> “(iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations;”

The draft contains no exception for disproportionate effects on the Company.

### Buyer replacement language

Replace clauses (ii) and (iii) of the definition of “Material Adverse Effect” with the following:

> **(ii)** changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry, **except to the extent such changes disproportionately affect the Company relative to other participants in the environmental services industry**;
>
> **(iii)** changes in Environmental Laws or regulations, **except to the extent such changes disproportionately affect the Company relative to other participants in the environmental services industry**;

All other portions of the definition remain unchanged.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The environmental-services and regulatory carve-outs cannot be absolute in this transaction. Cascadia’s value is directly tied to environmental regulation and environmental-services demand; an industry-wide or regulatory change that disproportionately harms Cascadia must remain available to support the MAE closing condition. This correction is required by **Playbook § 2.1** and the partner’s October 23 instructions. It also protects the buyer from precisely the sector-specific risks identified in the **DD Memo §§ I and V**.

---

## 3.2 Indemnification Cap definition

**Priority: Critical**

### Seller draft

> “**Indemnification Cap**” means Forty-Three Million Dollars ($43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.

### Buyer replacement language

> “**Indemnification Cap**” means **Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars ($26,875,000), which is equal to twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value**.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The Seller draft changes a binding economic term. Section 8 of the executed Term Sheet fixes the general cap at 12.5% of the $215,000,000 Base Enterprise Value, or $26,875,000. The 20% / $43,000,000 figure is not a negotiated alternative; it is a direct deviation from the binding term sheet. See **Term Sheet § 8** and **Playbook §§ 5.1 and 14 (Checklist Item 3)**.

---

# 4. Article II — Purchase price, earnout, and closing mechanics

## 4.1 Earnout covenant — eliminate affirmative operating obligations

**Priority: Critical**

### Seller draft

Section 2.05(d) provides:

> “From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. Without limiting the foregoing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action that would reasonably be expected to reduce the Adjusted EBITDA of the Company below the levels that would otherwise have been achieved. In furtherance of the foregoing, during the Earnout Period, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources as in effect immediately prior to the Closing Date and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates.”

### Buyer replacement language

Delete Section 2.05(d) in its entirety and replace it with:

> **(d) Operation of the Business During the Earnout Period.** Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action **with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment**. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05(d) shall restrict Buyer’s right to operate, integrate, restructure, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer’s sole discretion, including the right to make capital expenditure decisions, change pricing, make personnel decisions, make strategic investments, acquire or dispose of businesses or assets, enter new markets, discontinue or modify product or service lines, allocate corporate overhead, combine the Company with Buyer or any Affiliate, or make other operational modifications. No such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05(d) unless taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. Buyer shall have no obligation to maintain the Company as a separate entity, maintain any particular level of personnel, equipment, or capital expenditures, retain any particular employee, refrain from diverting or redirecting any contract, customer, revenue, or business opportunity, or operate the Company in a manner consistent with past practice.

### Track-changes comment

**Buyer comment:** The Seller’s language would restrict integration, restructuring, personnel, capital allocation, pricing, and strategic decisions throughout the earnout period and would create litigation over ordinary post-closing business judgment. The executed Term Sheet expressly requires only a negative covenant against actions taken with the **primary purpose** of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. The replacement tracks **Term Sheet § 5 (Earnout Covenant)** and **Playbook § 7.2**. It is also consistent with the firm’s PE-buyer position that the buyer does not owe an affirmative duty to maximize an earnout.

---

## 4.2 Earnout financial mechanics and Adjusted EBITDA

**Priority: High**

### Seller draft

The draft provides:

> “Adjusted EBITDA” means net income determined under GAAP applied consistently with past practice, plus interest, taxes, and depreciation and amortization, and further adjusted to exclude “(i) non-recurring transaction costs,” “(ii) purchase-price accounting adjustments,” “(iii) extraordinary or non-recurring items,” and “(iv) any management fees, monitoring fees, or similar fees charged by Buyer or any of its Affiliates.”

Section 2.05(c) provides that Buyer delivers the Earnout Statement **within sixty (60) days** after the end of the Earnout Period. Section 2.05(e) provides that payment is due **within ten (10) Business Days after final determination**.
